title: Oldest readings see a withdrawal the call ends

phrase.meaning: O you wrapped in your cloak

points.label: Fear and withdrawal
points.text: In **Jabir’s report**, the Prophet hears a voice, goes to Khadija and asks to be wrapped up; then Surah 74 comes. Rubin finds that readings of the cloak as **hiding, sleep or reluctance** look like the earliest layer.

points.label: A soothsayer’s mantle
points.text: **Nöldeke–Schwally**, followed by Buhl and Watt, linked the title to pre-Islamic **kāhins** who prophesied wrapped up. Rubin notes this reading is **absent from Muslim commentaries**: a modern comparative hypothesis.

points.label: Wrapped in prophethood
points.text: **ʿIkrima** (d. 723) read the cloak as a burden to carry; later **al-Rāzī** and **al-Ālūsī** call the Prophet covered in prophethood, knowledge and mercy: a title of honour.
points.who: ʿIkrima; al-Rāzī; al-Ālūsī, cited by Rubin

bottom_text: No full consensus. In the tafsir, the evidence leans to withdrawal, which “Arise!” ends; the honorific sense looks later. The kāhin link remains a plausible outside hypothesis, unattested in tafsir.
